newsitem.title: USA: US, Canada meet June 27 on grains dispute - USTR.
newsitem.headline: US, Canada meet June 27 on grains dispute - USTR.

text.p: U.S. and Canadian officials will meet June 27 in Ottawa for a new discussions of grain trade between the nations, U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Wednesday.

Farmers in the northern U.S. plains have complained for years of unfair imports of Canadian wheat. The Clinton administration has told Canada it would act if the shipments exceeded more than 1.5 million tonnes a year.
"We actually have a number of proposals on the table, including with respect to market access into Canada," Barshefsky said. "These proposals will be discussed.
"We hope to see some progress made," she said.
Canada has told the United States that it doubts shipments to U.S. buyers will exceed 1.5 million tonnes but it refuses to recognize any constraint on sales.
During a hearing, members of the Senate Agriculture Committee asked Barshefsky and Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman to seek removal of high Canadian tariffs on U.S. dairy products.
"We intend to do everything possible to eliminate" the barriers, Glickman responded.
Barshefsky said the U.S. International Trade Commission was reviewing potato trade between the nations following complaints of unfairly low-priced Canadian exports.
The United States challenged Canada's limits on dairy, poultry and livestock imports but lost the case before a North American Free Trade Agreement panel.
